clue.text: Know-all's telegram about cracked case

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', a link; the definition is the noun phrase

indicators.note: about means going round, so the telegram word surrounds the rest

parts.note: a wire is an old word for a telegram

indicators.note: something cracked is broken apart, so the letters of case are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who knows it all sends a telegram about a case that has been solved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracked' is the anagram signal and 'about' the container signal; 'Know-all's' is the definition with 's as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A smart alec who pretends to know everything is a synonym for a know-all.

clue.text: Short dramatist, eccentric, an unpredictable element

indicators.note: short means cut off before the end, so the surname loses its final letter

parts.note: Oscar Wilde was an Irish dramatist
a card is an eccentric or amusing person

explanation.surface: A playwright described as small and odd seems to be the unpredictable one.
explanation.definitionFit: A joker or unknown factor that could change things is called this, from card games.

clue.text: Small step in room

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a pace is a single step

explanation.surface: Taking a short step inside a room.
explanation.definitionFit: Room in the sense of available area or capacity is a synonym.

clue.text: Notice groom making formal speech

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement
to dress is to groom, as with hair or a horse

explanation.surface: Someone notices a bridegroom delivering a formal speech at a wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: An oration delivered to an audience on an occasion is a synonym.

clue.text: Travel about, carrying papers

indicators.note: carrying means holding something inside, so the about word holds the papers word

parts.note: re means about or concerning
ID, identity documents, are one's papers

explanation.surface: Travelling around while carrying documents.
explanation.definitionFit: To journey on a horse or in a vehicle is to go by transport, a synonym.

clue.text: Conservative rebels in times of intense difficulty

parts.note: rises means revolts or rebels, as in rising up

explanation.surface: A Tory rebellion during a period of political turmoil.
explanation.definitionFit: Emergencies or turning points of great trouble are what the plural noun names.

clue.text: Crack again? This could show strength of character

definitions.meaning: to crack a problem is to solve it, so doing it again is to solve it a second time

explanation.surface: Wondering whether solving something twice shows grit.
explanation.definitionFit: Determination and firmness of purpose are synonyms for strength of character; the first sense splits as RE plus SOLVE.

clue.text: One watching actor step out

indicators.note: out here means wrong or not in place, signalling the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An audience member watches as a performer steps off stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' is the anagram signal on ACTOR STEP.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who looks on at an event is an onlooker, an observer.

clue.text: Round taken into parlour in bar

indicators.note: taken into means placed inside, so the round letter goes inside the parlour word

parts.note: a salon is a parlour or reception room
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A round of drinks is brought into the back room of a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A lounge or public room in a pub, and in the American West a drinking establishment.

clue.text: Counterfeit note everyone rejected? Not so in Welsh resort

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the word for everyone reads backwards

parts.note: all means everyone
a dud is a fake or counterfeit item
no is a denial meaning not so

explanation.surface: A fake banknote is turned down everywhere, yet not so in a seaside town in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns ALL into LLA; the pieces are then assembled in answer order.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaside holiday town on the North Wales coast, an example of a resort.

clue.text: Exceed available balance

parts.note: out can mean available, as a book that is out for sale
to weigh is to balance, as on scales

explanation.surface: Spending more than the funds available in an account.
explanation.definitionFit: To be greater in weight or importance than something is to surpass it.

clue.text: Bigwig in his wellingtons

indicators.note: in means the letters are found inside the following words

explanation.surface: An important man dressed in his rubber boots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to letters running across HIS WELLINGTONS. Wellingtons are rubber boots in British English.
explanation.definitionFit: A dandy or fashionable person of standing; slang for a toff or important figure.

clue.text: Bright clubs and bar

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games
a lever is a bar used to prise something

explanation.surface: Golf clubs and a metal bar described as shiny.
explanation.definitionFit: Bright in the sense of intelligent or quick-witted is a synonym.

clue.text: Fired back during fight? Not with this weapon!

indicators.note: during means within, so the reversed word sits inside the fight word

parts.note: a set-to is a fight or scuffle

indicators.note: back means turned round, so the word for fired reads backwards

parts.note: lit means set alight, fired

explanation.surface: A shot returned in a scrap, but not from this weapon, which cannot be fired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' signals the reversal and 'during' the insertion. The joke: a stiletto is a dagger, so nothing is fired from it.
explanation.definitionFit: A short dagger with a slender blade is an example of a weapon.

clue.text: Clear policy declaration, lacking nothing

indicators.note: lacking means without, so the following letter is dropped

parts.note: a manifesto is a party's published declaration of policy
O is the figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A party's policy statement that is transparent and has no gaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Obvious or plainly evident, as an adjective, matches clear.

clue.text: Check account suggesting restoration

parts.note: to rein, or a rein, is a check or restraint
a statement is an account, such as a bank statement

explanation.surface: Checking a bank statement that hints at a refund being returned.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting someone back in their former post is a synonym for restoration.

clue.text: Start school?

definitions.meaning: to set up or begin something, as a verb
an educational or research body, as a noun

explanation.surface: Wondering whether to found a school.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to initiate; as a noun it names an academic establishment, such as a college.

clue.text: Rescue riveter working on base of bridge

indicators.note: working here means being worked into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged
the base of a down word is its bottom, its last letter

explanation.surface: A riveter repairing the foot of a bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges RIVETER into RETRIEV; 'base of' gives E from bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: To recover or bring something back from loss is a synonym for rescue.

clue.text: Kent town: tourist being corrected about name

indicators.note: about means going around, so the rearranged letters surround the name letter
corrected means put right, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A visitor to Kent is put right about a place's name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrected' rearranges TOURIST BEING and 'about' wraps it round N. Kent is a county in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: A market town in north Kent on the Swale, an example of a town there.

clue.text: Extremely large bird, a kind with no tail

parts.note: a tit is a small bird

indicators.note: with no tail means the last letter is removed

parts.note: nice means kind

explanation.surface: A huge bird of a gentle sort that has lost its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no tail' trims NICE to NIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Gigantic, like the Titans of Greek myth, is a synonym for extremely large.

clue.text: Cops out, deployed to find sea creature

indicators.note: deployed means spread out and arranged, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Police are sent out to find something in the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: An eight-armed marine mollusc is an example of a sea creature.

clue.text: Admits wife is in on matter raised

indicators.note: is in means sits inside, so the wife letter goes inside the following word
raised in a down clue means read upwards, so the word goes backwards

parts.note: pus is matter from an infection

explanation.surface: Someone confesses that his wife is involved in a matter brought up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is in' signals the insertion; 'raised' reverses, as this is a down clue read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To confess or acknowledge, as a phrasal verb, matches admits.

clue.text: Painter from Wiltshire, one I dismissed in error

indicators.note: in error means wrongly, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Wiltshire is an English county, here only letters to be rearranged
one of the two I letters in the county name is removed

explanation.surface: An artist from Wiltshire, having dismissed one in error.
explanation.walkthrough: Wiltshire is an English county; drop one I ('dismissed') and rearrange ('in error'). James McNeill Whistler was an American painter.
explanation.definitionFit: James McNeill Whistler, famous for his portrait of his mother, is an example of a painter.

clue.text: A daze caused by winning in shop once last one scratched

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the winning word goes within the shop word
once the last letter is scratched, meaning removed, the shop word is shortened

parts.note: a store is a shop
up means ahead, winning, as in being one up

explanation.surface: Feeling dazed after winning in a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once last one scratched' removes the final E, leaving STOR; 'in' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A dazed state of near unconsciousness is a synonym for a daze.

clue.text: Father and dean dropping first hymn

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: dropping first means the opening letter is removed

explanation.surface: A priest and a dean losing their place in a hymn.
explanation.definitionFit: A song of praise or triumph, so an example of a hymn.

clue.text: Sign of some nepotism

indicators.note: of here means taken out of, so the letters come from within the next words

explanation.surface: An indication of some favouritism.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across SOME NEPOTISM.
explanation.definitionFit: A portent or augury is a sign of things to come.

clue.text: Reject incentive offered by knight

parts.note: a spur is an incentive
N is the chess abbreviation for knight

explanation.surface: Turning down a reward offered by a knight.
explanation.definitionFit: To scorn or rebuff is a synonym for reject.

clue.text: Watch, for example, featured in American magazine article

parts.note: Time is an American news magazine
a piece is an article in a publication

explanation.surface: A wristwatch features in an American magazine article.
explanation.definitionFit: A clock or watch is an example of a device for measuring hours.

clue.text: Foremost of priests come to deliver a sermon

indicators.note: foremost means first in line, so the opening letter is taken

parts.note: to reach is to come to a place

explanation.surface: The leading priest arrives to give a sermon.
explanation.definitionFit: To give a religious address from the pulpit is to sermonise.

clue.text: Sort of trendy when seen dancing

parts.note: in means fashionable, trendy
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: dancing means moving about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone fashionable when spotted on the dance floor.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means partly or to some extent, which is what sort of conveys.
